title: Make a decision

outcomes.can: Predict which branch of an if, else if, else chain runs.
Tell = from == and read the error when they are mixed up.
Handle two separate conditions, including empty text and zero.

intro: A program becomes useful when it can choose. This module covers if and else, the comparison operators, and combining true/false values with and, or and not.

steps.title: Compare, then choose
steps.text: A comparison produces a bool. open > limit is true when open is larger. The comparison operators are == (equal), != (not equal), <, <=, > and >=. An if statement runs its block only when the condition in the brackets is true. else if tries another condition when the ones above were false. else runs when none matched. Only one block in the chain runs. Two strings are equal with == when they hold the same characters, and "" is a real string with no characters in it.

steps.title: Which branch runs?
steps.text: Read the if chain and predict the first line of output.

steps.title: Follow the chain
steps.text: open is 3 and limit is 3. open > limit is false, so the first block is skipped. open == limit is true, so "full" prints and the else block is skipped. The order of the tests matters: the chain stops at the first true condition.

steps.title: Combine conditions
steps.text: && means and: true only when both sides are true. || means or: true when at least one side is true. ! means not: it flips true and false. Predict the last two lines.

steps.title: Work out each side
steps.text: urgent is true and blocked is false, so !blocked is true and urgent && !blocked is true. open >= 5 is false, but urgent is true, so the || is true. Work out each side first, then combine them.

steps.title: Predict a comparison error
steps.text: One character is missing from this condition. Read it before checking.

steps.title: Read the compiler error
steps.text: Check the example. A single = assigns. open = 3 stores 3 and produces an int, and an if needs a bool, so the compiler reports CS0029. To compare, write ==.

steps.title: Report the board status
steps.text: The case boxes supply open and limit. The starter handles one rule and has the edge wrong. Change it so every case gets the right status.

steps.title: Decide whether work can start
steps.text: Work from the prompt. Every case supplies a different mix of values.

questions.prompt: What is the first line of output?

choices.feedback: 3 is not greater than 3, so the first condition is false.
The first test is false and the second is true, so its block runs.
else runs only when every condition above it was false.

questions.prompt: What are the last two lines of output?

choices.feedback: urgent is true and blocked is false. In the second line one true side is enough for ||.
open >= 5 is false, but || needs only one true side, and urgent is true.
!blocked flips false to true, so both sides of the && are true.

questions.prompt: What happens when you check this example?

choices.feedback: open = 3 is an assignment, not a comparison, and the compiler rejects it as a condition.

choices.text: It prints nothing, because the condition is false.
choices.feedback: The file never runs. The condition is not a bool at all.

choices.text: The compiler reports an error on line 2.
choices.feedback: A single = assigns and produces an int. An if needs a bool, so this is CS0029.

review.evidence: Open a fresh starter on a later visit, with the earlier answer closed. A first unaided pass on every case is later evidence of the skill. A hinted pass stays recorded as assisted.

drillGap: These drills practise one statement or operator each. They do not check an answer against several supplied cases.
